target.title: Feature/Fix: Integrate lineage discovery and shadow accounting
target.body:
## Stack dependency

This is PR 2 of 4. It follows [PR #2155](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2155); review and merge that PR first.

## Summary

Integrates bounded lineage discovery, token-accounting dimensions, and shadow execution with the existing scanner.

- pulls exceptional long-lived parents outside the normal scan window only when referenced by an included descendant
- indexes physical filename owners for parent discovery; retained metadata aliases cannot suppress the actual parent
- preserves UTC/local-day, model, cached-input, output, pricing, and physical-owner dimensions
- runs privacy-safe lineage comparison after refreshed legacy scans
- keeps the legacy report and cache authoritative
- contains non-cancellation shadow failures without changing production output

## Validation

- focused discovery, ledger, and shadow suites, including retained-parent metadata regression coverage
- redacted frozen-history replay summarized in PR #2158
- `make check`
- full suite: 650 selections across 55 groups; no failures, retries, or timeouts
- repository review gate: no material findings after fixes

Related investigation: [#2037](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2037).

target.title: Feature/Fix: Add a shadow lineage ledger for Codex token accounting
target.body:
## Summary

Adds the first isolated component of a planned Codex scanner rearchitecture: a typed lineage ledger plus an adapter from the existing fast JSONL parser.

The ledger treats rollout files as overlapping physical views of transitive session families. It now carries a copy-stable logical event identity derived from the turn and token-event ordinal. Physical copies collapse by that identity, unchanged ancestor/descendant re-emissions remain deduplicated, and independent equal-looking sibling events remain additive.

This PR does not change production totals. It establishes the accounting boundary used by the three follow-up PRs.

## Stack

1. **This PR:** ledger foundation and parser adapter
2. [Discovery, accounting dimensions, and shadow execution](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2156)
3. [Conservative evidence, bounded processing, and promotion controls](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2157)
4. [Real-world validation, diagnostics, and performance](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/pull/2158)

## Validation

- focused lineage ledger/parser tests, including copied and independent equal-looking events
- redacted frozen-history replay summarized in PR #2158
- `make check`
- full suite: 650 selections across 55 groups; no failures, retries, or timeouts
- repository review gate: no material findings after fixes

Related investigation: [#2037](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/issues/2037).

target.title: fix: prioritize exhausted Antigravity quota in menu bar and highest usage
target.body:
## Summary

- keep exhausted Antigravity five-hour quota buckets visible instead of falling back to a less-constrained weekly quota
- use reset-aware automatic menu-bar selection and maximum-usage ranking for their distinct consumers
- recognize every current session bucket ID spelling emitted by the provider parser: `-5h`, `-5-hour`, `-five-hour`, and `-session`
- keep the branch limited to five production/test files; remove the unrelated Linux platform-test serialization

## Why

When a five-hour Antigravity quota is exhausted but the weekly quota remains available, the reset that actually blocks work must remain visible in the menu bar and the provider must remain eligible for highest-usage ranking.

## Real consumer proof

A freshly built test binary executed the actual production resolver and `UsageStore` highest-usage consumer with an Antigravity snapshot:

```text
Antigravity production selection proof: resetFocused=30.0% highestUsage=95.0%
```

This demonstrates the intentionally distinct results:

- menu-bar automatic selection shows the next actionable reset window;
- the highest-usage consumer ranks the most constrained quota window.

The focused suite also covers exhausted five-hour buckets with usable weekly buckets, all-blocked-family detection, unsupported cadences, and all supported five-hour ID spellings. It contains no account, token, or session data.

## Validation

- `swiftformat Sources/CodexBar/MenuBarMetricWindowResolver.swift Tests/CodexBarTests/MenuBarMetricWindowResolverTests.swift`
- `swift test --scratch-path /private/tmp/codexbar-antigravity-build --skip-build --filter 'MenuBarMetricWindowResolverTests|UsageStoreHighestUsageTests'` — 53 tests passed
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `make check` completed repository scripts, locale, documentation, and initial lint checks, then stalled downloading its pinned SwiftFormat binary; CI has been restarted for the full hosted check.

target.title: ci: defer macOS tests for draft pull requests
target.body:
## Summary
- defer macOS Swift shards for code-changing Draft PRs while retaining Linux lint/build checks
- report Draft deferral as a successful aggregate check with an explicit workflow summary, rather than presenting the policy as a CI failure
- re-run CI when a PR becomes ready for review or returns to Draft
- make the Kiro detached-child timing fixture return and assert parseable context output, so its 8-second bound measures PTY cleanup rather than an empty optional-context probe timing out

## Why
Independent code PR batches can exhaust the scarce hosted macOS runner queue. A Draft PR is already unmergeable, so it should receive fast portable feedback and a clear deferred-validation state, then consume macOS capacity only when promoted for review.

The Kiro timing failure was concrete: the fixture exited with empty `/context` output, while `fetch()` subsequently performs an optional context probe with an 8-second bound. That made the test's own `< 8s` assertion contradictory. This change preserves the strict bound and validates parsed context usage instead of relaxing the timeout.

## Safety
- `ready_for_review` starts a fresh workflow where code changes again require both macOS Swift shards to pass
- `converted_to_draft` starts a new run in the same concurrency group, canceling queued or running macOS work for that branch
- a code-changing Draft PR can be green only for completed portable checks; the workflow summary records that macOS validation is deferred
- non-draft PRs and pushes to `main` retain the existing macOS path gate
- no test retries, timeout relaxations, or required-gate weakening

## Validation
- `bash Scripts/test_ci_path_gate.sh`
- `bash Scripts/test_swift_test_sharding.sh`
- GitHub Actions YAML parse and shell syntax checks
- exact repaired test: `swift test --filter 'CodexBarTests.KiroStatusProbeTests/`fetch returns promptly when usage helper spawns a detached child`'`
- `git diff --check`

## Follow-up identified during validation
The broader `KiroStatusProbeTests` suite still has a separate, pre-existing failure in `accepted pipe output cannot overrun the usage deadline`: a PTY marker file remains after the deadline assertion. This PR does not hide it or add retries; it should be reproduced and fixed as its own process-cleanup regression.
